build.summary:
I built access-femoral-puncture: the Brilakis femoral sequence before the sheath (marker on the femoral head, ultrasound scan, puncture, needle and micro-wire events) in the full case.

- **Site anatomy (`site.ts`).** New overrides: near-wall depth presets (20 and 40 mm), femoral head centre, anterior-wall calcium, inferior epigastric and lateral circumflex iliac origins, accessory profunda, small CFA. A calcified stretch narrows the target window to the longest clear stretch. New helpers: `calcifiedAt` and `entryVsHead` (below / lower half / upper half / above the head).
- **Needle and B-mode (`ultrasound.ts`).** A needle meeting calcified wall tents further and then glances off sideways. A plugged needle gives no blood until `flushNeedle()`. Once the 0.018 inch micro-wire runs free it takes a course: up the iliac, into the inferior epigastric (high entry, aimed medially), the lateral circumflex iliac (high, aimed laterally), down the leg (steep, near the bifurcation), or the course a scenario scripts. In a small branch it stops after a short run (wire-resistance). Pulled back below the turn, it goes up the artery when advanced again. The image shows calcium as a bright anterior arc with a shadow beneath, and draws the two branches.
- **Groin on fluoroscopy (`route.ts`).** `siteToAortic` maps the ultrasound site frame into the fluoroscopy frame. `limbExtras(r, model, site)` now places the femoral head from the site landmarks; without a site it draws as before. New drawing helpers put the femoral angiogram, the sheath, the needle, the micro-wire and the skin marker at their real site position.
- **Session (`caseSession.ts`).**
  - New marker and needle methods: `placeFemoralMarker`, `markFemoralHead`, `femoralMarkX`, `flushNeedle`, and `scriptAccess` for scenario scripts.
  - `CASE_SESSION_EVENTS` gains wire-resistance, wire-misdirected and wrong-height. `caseTips.ts` already builds its `raises` from that list, so it was not touched.
  - Screening the groin with the micro-wire in (`noteFluoroscopy('groin')`) raises wire-misdirected and wrong-height. A plugged needle with its tip in a lumen raises no-flashback.
  - A sheath over a misplaced micro-wire is refused as a critical stop; the attending's line does not name the branch.
  - Four new scored decisions: head marked, deep-artery angle and skin entry, entry over the head and above the bifurcation within two passes, and sheath over a misplaced wire.
  - An accessory profunda stick is no longer described as "below the bifurcation".
- **Autopilot.** It marks the head, flushes a plugged needle, screens and redirects a misplaced micro-wire, and takes out a wrong-height wire that a start state left in. `advanceToFlash` now defaults to the needle's full length. All ten scenarios reach 'sheath-in' with no critical error and no failed femoral decision.
- **Scenarios.** `femoral.ts` and `femoral.launch.ts` add ten scenarios, each opening ready to puncture. `fem-entry-below-head` is linked from pm-access-femoral-sheath at the fluoroscopy workspace.
- **UI.** The fluoroscopy view gets a "Marker" hand (drag on the image) and a "Mark the skin here" button; it draws the head, sheath, needle and micro-wire at the groin, only on exposed frames, and names neither the wire's course nor the entry height. The ultrasound view gets "Take out and flush the needle", wire pull-back and feed after the needle is out at the groin, "21 gauge" and "0.018 inch" labels, and a depth range up to 80 mm.

build.notes:
I snapshotted all 8 existing listed files into datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/access-femoral-puncture/ and created .started before editing. femoral.ts and femoral.launch.ts are new. Since the start, other packages changed planning.ts, planning.test.ts and files under src/ui/lab and src/ui/pci; this package did not touch them.

Places where I interpreted the design:

- **The two branches** (inferior epigastric, lateral circumflex iliac) are in `AccessSite.branches`, not in `tubes`. They appear on ultrasound and steer the micro-wire, but the needle model does not puncture them (they arise above the ligament). This keeps every existing femoral site, needle result and B-mode test unchanged.
- **Calcium blocks entry.** "Needles through calcium tent and deflect" is modelled as: the calcified wall never gives; once the needle has tented it, it glances off sideways (yaw changes). The learner has to choose a clear stretch.
- **"SFA when caudal"** became: a needle at 50 degrees or steeper entering within 8 mm above the bifurcation sends the wire down the leg. The scenario script also forces any course; a scripted turn is used once.
- **Steep femoral needle.** The existing wire rule (no wire through a needle steeper than 58 degrees) would make Brilakis's second option (about 70 degrees) impossible. I added `wireSteepDegFemoral` = 75 for femoral sites only; the radial limit is unchanged.
- **wrong-height** is raised for an entry below or above the femoral head, matching the lesson's high and low rows; an entry over the upper half of the head is not flagged. The femoral-entry decision counts "over the head" as either half.
- **wire-resistance** is raised for any wire resistance at the needle, at both groin and wrist. No tip uses that event today, so no panel changes.
- **Drawing.** The micro-wire is drawn with the scene builder's existing "014" wire, the thinnest available. The sheath at a femoral site runs from the skin through the arteriotomy to the route's start. Drawing sizes are labelled MODEL PARAMETER.
- **Autopilot.** It marks the head only when fluoroscopy is in use, so the crossover test's "no fluoroscopy" case still marks nothing. Femoral cases from all starts now carry the new decisions, and the autopilot scores them as expected.

review.verdict:
Approve, with seven minor fixes. I found nothing critical or major. The package is implemented completely: the site overrides and landmarks, calcium (bright arc, shadow, tent then glance off), the plugged needle and flushNeedle, the micro-wire course rule and scripts, branch resistance with pull-back and re-advance, siteToAortic and limbExtras placing the head from the landmarks (the no-site fallback is unchanged), the groin drawing, the marker hand and the 'Mark the skin here' button, the critical stop for a sheath over a misplaced wire, four new ledger decisions, the autopilot changes, and ten scenarios with their launch file.

**Tests and typecheck.** I ran these myself:
- The three package test files: 46 of 46 passed.
- Neighbouring session tests (caseSession, multiSite, scenarios): 56 of 57 passed. The one failure is 'clean case' in scenarios.test.ts, a radial case. Its only failed decision is pre-puncture-checklist from modules/planning.ts, which another package changed at 09:10.
- multiSite.tips, handover, ledgerTips, caseTips, caseTips.reach, siteSelector and planning: 84 of 84 passed.
- npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit: clean.

**Files changed outside the list.** Files changed since .started that are not on the package list sit under src/ui/pci, src/ui/lab, src/simulation/patient, and planning.ts / planning.test.ts. Other packages plausibly changed them.

**Browser check (in the dev pane on port 5173).** I opened fem-micro-wire-iea from the scenario picker, marked the head, punctured and fed the micro-wire. The course was 'iea' and wireMisdirected() was true. wire-misdirected was not active before an exposed frame and was raised after `__accessFluoroDraw({station:'groin'})`. The draw took about 49 ms, and there were no console errors. I could not read back the WebGL pixels (the drawing buffer is not preserved), so I did not see the marker over the head or the IEA wire medially with my own eyes. That geometry rests on the headless tests and on the code: the new parts are drawn only after the `!on` early return, so they appear only with the beam on. The dev pane is still on that scenario.

**Content and wording.**
- No ground truth appears on live screens: the attending lines name neither the branch nor the height, and the course goes only to telemetry.
- The cited numbers check out against 05-access.ts and pm-access.json: the 45 and 70 degree options, 'first or second pass', 'needle plugged', the accessory profunda, 21 gauge and 0.018 inch. Everything else is labelled MODEL PARAMETER.
- British English and the design-system classes (btn, btn-ghost, seg-btn) are used throughout.

**For the orchestrator (out of scope here).**
- docs/realism/facts/C5.md does not exist at all, though site.ts and the builder's report both point to it. Someone needs to create it with the new MODEL PARAMETERS.
- In every femoral scenario the pre-puncture-checklist decision still fails under the autopilot, and in supervised or exam mode the planning module refuses placeNeedle. The planning package owns both.

After that the marker is never drawn, 'Mark the skin here' stays disabled, and decideHeadMarked never fires for the learner's own repeat puncture. The scenario expects the learner to puncture again over the head, but they cannot use the marker or be scored on it.

A cleaner alternative: in AccessFluoroView, gate the marker drawing and the button on 'no needle in the skin and no wire' (`!(pst.needle && pst.needle.inserted > 0) && !pst.wire && !act.sheath`) instead of firstPassAt, and in caseSession score the head marker at the first skin pass after a start state (record that a start state ran, and score at the next pass). Add a test: open fem-entry-below-head, abandonPass, placeFemoralMarker(headFrom), markFemoralHead returns true, puncture, then femoral-head-marked is correct.

findings.problem: The critical stop fires whenever wireMisdirected() is true, even with the needle still in. pm.insertSheath would refuse that anyway with the ordinary technique line. So clicking the sheath with the needle still in is scored as a critical error for an action that could not have happened.
findings.fix: Change the condition to `this.activeSite.siteKind === "femoral" && this.pm.st.needleRemoved && this.pm.wireMisdirected()`. Add a test: in fem-micro-wire-iea, insertSheath with the needle still in returns false with criticalErrors 0; after removeNeedle it is the critical stop.

findings.problem: When the needle glances off calcium, the code wipes the wall state of every vessel on the pass, not just the target. If the needle had already entered another vessel on this pass (for example the CFV), the next step registers that front wall again. veinPunctures goes up twice, holes are duplicated and a second front-wall event is sent.
findings.fix: Reset only the target's wall: replace `this.st.walls = {}; this.wall(t.id).glanced = true;` with `this.st.walls[t.id] = { frontTent: 0, backTent: 0, frontHole: false, backHole: false, roll: 0, glanced: true };` (use the WallState constructor the file already uses in wall()). Keep the crossings recompute.

findings.problem: The 75 degree wire limit applies to every femoral-kind site, including femoral-vein and added crossover sites that this package does not own. That changes shared-engine behaviour for labs it does not touch: a 60 to 75 degree needle there used to meet 'steep' resistance. The justification (Brilakis's 70 degree option) covers the deep common femoral artery only.
findings.fix: Scope it to the femoral artery target: `const femArtery = this.site.kind === "femoral" && this.site.arteryId === "cfa"; const steep = n.angleDeg > (femArtery ? MP_NEEDLE.wireSteepDegFemoral : MP_NEEDLE.wireSteepDeg);`. Add a test that a 65 degree needle at a femoral-vein site still gives wire-resistance reason 'steep'.

fix.notes:
I checked all 7 findings against the code, applied every one, and rejected none. Two were applied in a changed form, explained under 1 and 4. All 51 package tests and 60 neighbouring tests pass, and the typecheck is clean. I edited only files on the package list plus its test files.

1. **fem-entry-below-head marker** (`scenarios/femoral.ts`, `AccessFluoroView.tsx`). `wireInBelowTheHead` now ends with `s.activeSite.firstPassAt = null`, so the learner's own first skin pass is the one scored on the head marker. I also took the reviewer's view-side option: a new `markerAllowed(act)` helper gates both the marker drawing and the "Mark the skin here" button. It requires that the site has had no skin pass yet, no needle is in the skin, and there is no wire or sheath. I did not add a separate "a start state ran" flag to `caseSession`; the scenario reset is enough because `openAtStart` already clears the autopilot's decisions. New test: open the scenario, `abandonPass`, place the marker on `headFrom`, mark, puncture; `femoral-head-marked` is correct.

2. **insertSheath critical stop** (`caseSession.ts`). The misplaced-wire stop now also requires `this.pm.st.needleRemoved`. With the needle still in, the click gets the ordinary technique line and no critical error. New test in fem-micro-wire-iea: with the needle in, the sheath is refused, there are 0 critical errors and no decision is recorded; after `removeNeedle` it is the critical stop.

3. **Calcium deflection** (`ultrasound.ts`). Only the target's wall is reset now: `this.st.walls[t.id] = { ...newWall(), glanced: true }`. The crossings are still recomputed. New test: a CFV wall state set by hand during the pass survives the glance, and `veinPunctures` stays 0.

4. **Steep wire limit** (`ultrasound.ts`). The reviewer's exact fix (`site.arteryId === "cfa"`) would have changed nothing, because every femoral-kind site has `arteryId` "cfa", including added crossover sites. There is no femoral-vein site kind. I scoped the limit to the vessel the bevel opens into instead: `femArtery = site.kind === "femoral" && !!t && t.id === site.arteryId`. The CFV and the branches therefore keep the shared default of 58 degrees. Crossover sites keep the 75 degree limit, because they are also the common femoral artery and the Brilakis reasoning applies to them. New test: a 65 degree needle in the CFV gives wire-resistance with reason "steep", and the same angle in the CFA passes.

5. **Which half of the femoral head** (`caseSession.ts`). Scoring is unchanged. Both `decideFemoralEntry` and `decideDeepEntry` now say "over the lower/upper half of the femoral head" in the debrief text. The `expected` text now reads "Arterial entry over the femoral head (its lower half unless a high bifurcation leaves only the upper half), above the bifurcation ...". New test checks both texts on the redone entry.

6. **Per-frame allocations.**
   - `ultrasound.ts`: `renderBMode` now takes its tube list from `imagedTubes(site)`, which builds it once per site and keeps it in a module-level WeakMap. I checked that `site.tubes` and `site.branches` are never changed after the site is built.
   - `site.ts`: `calcifiedAt` is now a plain for loop.
   - `AccessFluoroView.tsx`: the draw loop keeps each sheath's tube in a per-site `sheathCache`, rebuilt only when the route geometry, site, sheath, arteriotomy x or needle angle changes. The groin marker, needle and micro-wire are kept in `groinCache`, rebuilt only when a signature string, the route geometry or the site changes. I checked that `buildXrayScene` only reads these tubes.

7. **Tautological test** (`access.test.ts`). I ran the snapshot `site.ts` from `datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/access-femoral-puncture` against the new one using vite-node from the scratchpad. For seeds fp-same and fp-gold the two sites were identical once calcium, branches and `landmarks.headX` were removed. I then pinned the fp-same values in the test: fat depth, CFA radius and depth at x=0, ligament and bifurcation positions, head edges, tube ids, typical angle, and the femoral-head bone.

   - AccessSiteState gains `markerSeenX` and `markSeen`.

FIELD_MM is the field at the detector, scaled back to the isocentre. So the marker follows the pointer at any canvas size.

   - If the wire was screened: 'Stop. That wire is not where it should be: pull it back and redirect it before anything goes over it.'
